layers.label: Education ahead of employment
layers.question: Where are women’s education outcomes furthest ahead of their employment opportunity?
layers.direction: Higher means education advantage exceeds employment advantage
layers.source: Derived from latest gender-specific education and employment composites
layers.caveat: Different indicators may refer to different years and cohorts; this is not an individual transition measure.
layers.short_caveat: Indicators may cover different years and cohorts
layers.period: Latest available education and employment composites

layers.label: Opportunity conversion surprise
layers.question: Which countries perform better or worse on women’s employment opportunity than the model expects?
layers.direction: Negative means under-conversion; positive means above-model conversion
layers.caveat: A residual is a discovery signal, not a causal effect or a ranking of policy quality.
layers.short_caveat: Model residual; not a causal effect

layers.label: Education progress without employment progress
layers.question: Where did education gender gaps improve faster than employment gender gaps?
layers.direction: Higher means a larger conversion shortfall
layers.caveat: Endpoint comparisons are sensitive to coverage years and do not track the same cohort.
layers.short_caveat: Endpoint comparison; not the same cohort of women

layers.label: Gap momentum state
layers.question: Is the modeled gender opportunity gap closing, flat or widening?
layers.direction: Closing, Flat, or Widening
layers.caveat: Show state probabilities in the tooltip; the most likely state can still be uncertain.
layers.short_caveat: Model state; not a forecast guarantee

layers.label: Risk the employment gap remains sticky
layers.question: Where is the gap unlikely to halve even within 15 years?
layers.direction: Higher means greater modeled persistence
layers.caveat: Conditional on model assumptions and available historical observations.
layers.short_caveat: Conditional model probability, not a promise
layers.period: Simulated from the fitted historical process

layers.label: Data visibility
layers.question: For how many core opportunity domains do we have comparable data?
layers.direction: Higher means better observed coverage
layers.caveat: Coverage is not data quality; it only counts observed core domains.
layers.short_caveat: Coverage is not data quality
layers.period: Coverage audit of education, employment, finance and digital domains

layers.label: Education gender gap over time
layers.question: How far is girls' secondary enrollment from parity with boys'?
layers.direction: Negative means girls enrol less than boys; positive means girls enrol more
layers.caveat: Gross enrollment parity, not completion or learning; observed years only, gaps are shown as missing.
layers.short_caveat: Observed years only; enrollment is not completion

layers.label: Employment gender gap over time
layers.question: How far is women's labour-force participation from men's?
layers.direction: Negative means women participate less than men
layers.source: ILO modelled estimates via World Bank WDI (SL.TLF.CACT.FM.ZS)
layers.caveat: ILO modelled estimates, not direct observations; participation includes informal and vulnerable work.
layers.short_caveat: ILO modelled estimate; includes informal work

layers.label: Education–employment conversion gap over time
layers.question: In which years was education closer to gender parity than employment?
layers.direction: Higher means education is closer to parity than labour-force participation
layers.caveat: Shown only where an observed education value and a modelled employment value exist for the same year. Different age groups and cohorts; not a transition rate.
layers.short_caveat: Observed education vs modelled employment; different cohorts

layers.label: Women's labour-force participation over time
layers.question: What share of women aged 15+ are in the labour force?
layers.direction: Higher means more women in the labour force
layers.source: ILO modelled estimates via World Bank WDI (SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS)
layers.caveat: Participation is not job quality: it includes vulnerable, informal and unpaid family work.
layers.short_caveat: ILO modelled estimate; participation is not job quality

layers.label: Women's vulnerable employment over time
layers.question: What share of employed women are own-account or contributing family workers?
layers.direction: Higher means more of women's work is vulnerable
layers.source: ILO modelled estimates via World Bank WDI (SL.EMP.VULN.FE.ZS)
layers.caveat: ILO modelled estimates; a proxy for insecure work, not a direct measure of earnings or conditions.
layers.short_caveat: ILO modelled estimate

layers.label: Rural electricity gap over time
layers.question: How far does rural electricity access lag urban access?
layers.direction: Higher means rural households lag further behind urban households
layers.source: SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset via World Bank WDI (EG.ELC.ACCS.UR/RU.ZS)
layers.caveat: Household access applies to women and men alike; compiled from surveys and estimates. Context for time poverty, not a women-only outcome.
layers.short_caveat: Household context, not a women-only outcome

layers.label: Rural clean-cooking gap over time
layers.question: How far does rural access to clean cooking lag urban access?
layers.direction: Higher means rural households lag further behind urban households
layers.source: WHO estimates via World Bank WDI (EG.CFT.ACCS.UR/RU.ZS)
layers.caveat: Modelled household estimates; relevant to fuel-collection time but not a direct time-use measure.
layers.short_caveat: Modelled household estimate

layers.label: Financial inclusion gender gap
layers.question: Where is women’s account access furthest below men’s?
layers.direction: Negative indicates a female disadvantage
layers.caveat: Account ownership does not measure control over money or account usage.
layers.short_caveat: Account ownership is not control over money

layers.label: Digital access gender gap
layers.question: Where is women’s digital access furthest below men’s?
layers.direction: Negative indicates a female disadvantage
layers.caveat: Indicator definitions and observation years vary by country.
layers.short_caveat: Definitions and years vary by country
layers.period: Latest available year (not recorded in the package)

layers.label: Women with official identification
layers.question: Where might lack of legal identity constrain access to work, finance and services?
layers.direction: Higher means more women report official ID ownership
layers.source: Global Findex / ID4D via World Bank (ID.OWN.TOTL.FE.ZS), latest genuine wave
layers.caveat: Coverage is sparse and ID ownership does not guarantee usable or safe digital identity.
layers.short_caveat: Sparse coverage; ownership is not usable ID

layers.label: Women’s unpaid-care time tax
layers.question: Where do women spend the most additional hours per day on unpaid work relative to men?
layers.unit: female minus male hours per day
layers.direction: Higher means a larger female time burden
layers.caveat: Time-use data are sparse and survey instruments are not perfectly harmonized.
layers.short_caveat: Sparse, not fully harmonized time-use surveys

layers.label: Maternal mortality
layers.question: Where do severe maternal-health risks remain highest?
layers.direction: Higher means worse maternal-health outcomes
layers.caveat: Use a log scale for the legend because the cross-country distribution is strongly skewed.
layers.short_caveat: Modelled estimate; legend uses a log scale

layers.label: Rural time-tax infrastructure gap
layers.question: Where do rural households face the largest infrastructure access gap relevant to women’s time poverty?
layers.direction: Higher means a larger rural disadvantage
layers.caveat: This is a contextual household infrastructure measure, not an individual women-only outcome.
layers.short_caveat: Household infrastructure context, not a women-only outcome

layers.label: Probability the gap is widening
layers.question: Where is worsening momentum most probable?
layers.direction: Higher means stronger modeled evidence of widening
layers.caveat: Model probability, not a forecast guarantee.
layers.short_caveat: Model probability; not a forecast guarantee

layers.label: Chance of halving the employment gap within 10 years
layers.question: Where does the stochastic model indicate faster potential convergence?
layers.direction: Higher means greater modeled chance of reaching half the current gap
layers.caveat: Conditional on the fitted historical process; not a policy forecast.
layers.display_label: Chance of halving the employment gap within 10 years
layers.short_caveat: Conditional model probability, not a promise
layers.period: Simulated from the fitted historical process

layers.label: Asynchronous data years
layers.question: Where are the latest domain indicators drawn from very different years?
layers.direction: Higher means less temporally comparable domain data
layers.caveat: A large spread can make apparent cross-domain desynchronization partly a timing artifact.
layers.short_caveat: Large spreads limit comparability across domains
layers.period: Years between the oldest and newest core observation

layers.label: Data invisibility: observed education years
layers.question: In how many years since 1990 was girls' and boys' secondary enrollment actually observed?
layers.direction: Lower means the education record is thinner
layers.caveat: Counts observations, not data quality. Modelled series (e.g. ILO) are excluded.
layers.short_caveat: Counts observed years only

layers.label: Data invisibility: missing observed country-years
layers.question: What share of possible country-years are missing in observed gender-disaggregated series?
layers.direction: Higher means more of the record is missing
layers.source: Coverage of 4 observed education series (1990–2024) and women in management (2000–2024)
layers.caveat: Measures what is missing from observed statistics; modelled series are excluded because they are always complete.
layers.short_caveat: Observed gender-disaggregated series only
